meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 17: AAIF & Agentic Ecosystem (multi-select)
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Which statements about MCP's place in the AAIF are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Contributors keep their copyright; no assignment to the foundation is required
The foundation's board approves each specification revision before release
Foundation membership replaced the maintainer roles with elected seats
MCP runs as 'Model Context Protocol, a Series of LF Projects, LLC'
agentgateway joined the foundation after the launch, in June 2026

questions.explanation: The legal entity, contributor copyright retention and agentgateway's later arrival are all accurate. Revisions are approved through the project's own SEP and Core Maintainer process, and the maintainer ladder is unchanged and individual-based.

questions.question: Which statements about rolling MCP out across an enterprise are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: MCP defines the audit log format that connected servers must emit
A gateway can enforce policy centrally, helped by the routing headers
A registry entry helps teams discover a server but does not vouch for it
One server can serve many hosts, so integrations are written once
MCP supplies the identity provider, so no separate SSO is needed

questions.explanation: Reuse across hosts, central policy at a gateway using Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name, and discovery without endorsement are all real. MCP builds on OAuth 2.1 rather than providing an identity provider, and it defines no audit log format.
